content:
Devon: Quick heads-up — doing a short batch profiling pass on the v2 canary. seeing a p95 delta vs baseline, need a quick go/no-go from releases.
Ana: Can you paste the numbers + what config you ran?
Devon: baseline p95=180ms (batch=8, seq=256). canary p95=235ms same config. median shift smaller (~+20ms). not sure if it's noise or kernel regress.
Ryan: Oof 55ms p95 delta is non-trivial. Did you run with the same quant / kernel flags?
Devon: yep, same quant profile. command I ran:
```
python infra/bench/run_profile.py --model redwood-v2-quant --batch 8 --seq 256 --warmup 50 --iters 200 --out=out/canary_run.json
```
Maria: Can you upload the profile to the perf dashboard? link to baseline and canary would help.
Devon: uploaded both to /perf/benchmarks/1751234567 (shared in dashboard). also grabbed a flamegraph: `s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1751234567/flame.svg`
SRE-Matt: Any change in host-side CPU steal or GPU util during the run? those can spike p95.
Devon: GPU util stable 98-100%, CPU spike around 12% for kernel prep on canary hosts.
Ana: If CPU is the source, might be scheduling noise; but we shouldn't ignore a p95 bump at release gate. What's the impact on tail-latency SLOs?
Ryan: Our SLO is p95 < 200ms for that route. baseline was fine, canary fails. That means we can't auto-approve.
Devon: Agree. Proposal: trigger narrow bisect — run same profile across 3 canary variants (kernel A, kernel B, fallback). If kernel B restores baseline, we can proceed with a guarded rollout.
Maria: I can spin the 3 jobs. ETA ~20m. tagging @ops-bot to schedule.
ops-bot: Scheduled profiling jobs: job-175123-A, job-175123-B, job-175123-F at 1751234680. Results will post here when done.
SRE-Matt: Also add a synthetic traffic run at p50-p99 distribution; sometimes batching interactions surface only under mixed seq distribution.
Devon: good call — adding mixed-seq job. command:
```
python infra/bench/run_profile.py --model redwood-v2-quant --batch 8 --seq-mix "64:0.5,256:0.3,512:0.2" --warmup 50 --iters 300
```
Maria: jobs started. I'll post raw numbers here.
Ryan: For the release decision: if any variant stays >25% worse on p95 vs baseline, we rollback. if one variant is within 10%, we can canary with 10% traffic and close monitoring.
Devon: understood. I'll wait for results then call for votes.
(10m later) ops-bot: job-175123-A complete. p95=228ms. job-175123-B complete. p95=186ms. job-175123-F complete. p95=240ms. mixed-seq job complete. p95=210ms.
Maria: Looks like kernel B is within baseline margin. B is candidate.
SRE-Matt: Anyone comfortable approving staged rollout pinned to kernel B with 10% traffic and 5m observation windows? fallback to baseline model if p95 > 220ms during window.
Ana: +1 from infra. sounds safe. :thumbsup:
Ryan: +1 from releases, monitor p95 and error rates. set an automated rollback trigger.
Devon: +1 — I'll update rollout config and kick the staged rollout. Will post the rollout id and monitoring link.
ops-bot: Staged rollout started: rollout-175123. 10% -> 30% over 30m if no regressions. Rollback trigger: p95 > 220ms OR error-rate increase >0.2%.
Devon: Rollout id: rollout-175123. Monitoring: https://console/perf/rollouts/rollout-175123
Maria: I'll watch dashboards and ping here if something odd appears.
SRE-Matt: Good process. If we see flapping, we'll pause and collect traces.
Devon: Thanks all — closing this thread for now. If anyone sees issues ping me directly or reopen here. :partyparrot:
